title: Rabbi Chinena, Father of Rabbi Yinta
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim, at the beginning of chapter 4, he speaks in Rabbi Benayah’s name: “From where do we know that an ox is called atonement?” In Taanit 4:2 it reads “father of Bar Neta,” and there, halakhah 8, “father of Bar Yinta.” The supplied notice breaks off at “Possibly he is [1].”

notes.text: The supplied notice stops at “Possibly he is [1]”; neither continuation nor footnote is supplied. It reads השור, “the ox,” while the Guggenheimer digital Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 4:1 reads השיר, “the song,” and calls Chinena the father of Rav Yinta. The incomplete sentence remains held.

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. II, p. 472) reads “the song” (השיר) and continues: “Possibly he is Rabbi Chinena, father of Bar Yeshita, mentioned at the end of Megillah 4:10. Rabbi Abbahu spoke in his name, and his son Yeshita was Rabbi Abbahu’s interpreter.” This is Hyman’s proposed identification. The consulted Megillah 4:10 names Bar Yashita as Rabbi Acha’s interpreter and distinguishes what he heard from his father from reports in Rabbi Chinena’s name. In the consulted Taanit the Bar Yinta form occurs at 4:5, in the discussion of the fast.
